name: sram_cim_macro
display_name: Digital SRAM-CIM macro (16 nm, 128 kB, jiang2023a; macro-level constants only)

validity.array_size_assumed: 128 kB of 6T in 128 blocks of 1 kB (64 rows of 128 b); 16 SR groups of 8 blocks each compute one 128-input dot product per cycle, so the macro is one logical core of 128 inputs x 1024 weight vectors of 8-bit weights; 4-bit inputs, 32-bit partial sums, exact digital accumulation (jiang2023a p.2-3)
validity.notes: MACRO-LEVEL constants only, measured at 20 MHz and 0.58 V (jiang2023a p.4). Chip-level rows (periphery, NoC, host, static power, the cycle time of a whole evaluation) are absent and refuse by name; the backing store is declared by a backing-store override block (CL5, CL7), so an SRAM point is never read without it.

e_mac.derivation: 12.6 TOPS/W non-weight-stationary at 8b W x 4b A, 20 MHz: 2 / 12.6e12 J = 158.7 fJ per MAC (1 MAC = 2 OPs); weight-stationary with 20x reuse 23.8 TOPS/W = 84.0 fJ (the band's low end). The non-WS anchor is the one a CIM activation reads.

e_write_per_cell.derivation: An 8-bit weight cell is one byte; the array write per byte is bracketed between 1x the measured local-block read byte energy (76 fJ at 20 MHz) and 2x the 91 MHz value (342 fJ), a write being full swing where the read is half swing. Nominal at the log-space centre.
e_write_per_cell.note: houshmand2023benchmarking Table II and Fig. 7 p.6 carry an analytical weight-write term that was not read in this round; it is the cross-check this bracket waits on.

write_verify_iterations.derivation: A digital SRAM write is one full-swing write with no verify loop.

endurance_cycles.note: 'about 1e16 cycles over the expected lifetime of embedded SRAM' (scout_chip.md sec. 4.3, SOURCED).

external_components.name: backing store
external_components.note: the macro holds 128 kB of weights and no store for the rest of a program: the backing store sets the tile write cost (constants.md sec. 5: an 8 KiB tile write costs 0.62-7.7 nJ in the array and 1.33 uJ over DDR3/4 I/O), so an SRAM-CIM point is defined only with its store's transfer energy and time declared, by a named backing_store block
